To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the unique concept of materials nanarchitectonics can be utilized to fabricate high performance nanoporous carbon materials from synthetic biomass or agricultural waste precursors with controllable surface areas and hierarchical nanoporous structure for supercapacitors application.
the nanoarchitectonically designed hierarchical porous carbons are promising candidates for high performance supercapcitors.

nanoporous graphitic carbons with controllably designed surface area, pore volume and hierarchy in nanopore structure can be fabricated from single crystalline fullerenes and metal organic frameworks using hard and soft templation routes and from biomass and agricultural wastes using direct carbonization and activation methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing novel synthetic routes for the preparation of nanoporous carbon materials from biomass and agricultural waste sources for supercapacitors application.
the synthesis of high performance porous carbones with controlled pore structure and surface area for energy applications.
developing novel nanoporous carbon materials from biomass precursors for high performance supercapactors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the nanoarchitectonic approach of materials design for the fabrication of nanoporous carbon materials from biomass or agricultural wastes can be a promising strategy for the production of high performance supercapacs.
the synthetic routes of nanoporous carbons are not limited only to the use of biomass or agricultural waste materials.
the synthetic methods for hierarchical porous carbon materials are highly dependent on the carbon source and precursors used in the fabrication of the materials.

, the nanoarchitectonically designed nanoporous carbons with high surface area and large pores can be synthesized from various carbon precursors, such as biomass and agricultural wastes.
nanoporous carbons with hierarchical structure can be fabricated by different methods and the resulting materials can be used in supercapacitor applications.
the nanoarchitectonically designed hierarchical nanoporous carbon materials from natural precursors with high surface area and large volume can be used in high performance super capacitors.

nanoporous carbon materials derived from biomass or agricultural wastes are promising for the development of high performance supercapcitors.
the synthetic methods for accessing nanoporous carbons are highly promising in terms of their high surface area, high pore volume, and high pore size distribution.
the synthetic methods and carbon precursors used for the fabrication of high performance hierarchical porous carbon materials are highly dependent on the specific applications.
